subject: research/mimic-anycontext-detect
professional: an ML researcher who publishes on machine-generated-text detection and out-of-distribution generalisation (RAID, MAGE/DeepfakeTextDetect, M4 style cross-domain and cross-generator evaluations): first checks that the held-out split really is held out (no vectoriser, threshold or hyper-parameter fitted on the target), that comparisons use equal training budgets, that uncertainty covers the sampling of texts and not only the seed, and that the result is new against the cross-domain tables already in RAID and MAGE

evidence.correctness: Ran with /usr/bin/python3.13 (numpy, scipy, scikit-learn via platform/ci/pyenv.py). Recomputed three results with my own script (scratchpad recompute.py: my own Mann-Whitney rank AUROC, and a vectoriser fitted on the TRAINING families only, stricter than the author's whole-suite fit). (1) universal AUROC, books: mine 0.993 on the whole family, README/results.txt 0.993. (2) universal, recipes: mine 0.867 on the whole family against README 0.843 (mean over half-splits) and results.txt length-matched 'all' 0.855 (whole family, author's vectoriser); a 0.01 to 0.02 gap, so the number reproduces, and it moved UP when the target text was removed from the vectoriser, the opposite of the README's remark that the leak 'slightly favours the universal regime'. (3) universal, wiki: mine 0.895 against 0.896. (4) per-family wiki, seed 0, two folds: 0.955 and 0.929, mean 0.942, against the 5-seed mean 0.926 (sd 0.010), consistent for one seed. (5) length-alone AUROC: wiki 0.845 and poetry 0.115 match the README. Also recomputed from the shipped files: results.json means give mean universal 0.9337 and per-family 0.9850, gap +0.051, held-out-generator minimum 0.899 over 20 cells, the README's length-matched deltas (recipes -0.001, reddit -0.001, others +0.002 to +0.023) all match results.txt. No wrong number found. Limit: I did not rerun the 8-minute anyctx.py end to end, so the generator hold-out and adapted-k cells other than those above were checked only against results.json for internal consistency.
evidence.completeness: README claims and what I checked: 5 tests (ran, 5 pass); results table (matches results.txt/results.json); universal, per-family, adapted k = 10/40/160, held-out generator (20 cells, shipped) and length-matched control (shipped, code in anyctx.py); figure.py and experiments/figure.svg exist; live-page line and homepage entry present; the model-based part is explicitly not claimed. Stubs, TODOs or dead links: none found. 'Next steps' and 'Owner steps' are declared future work, and the prompted-detector half already exists as mimic-anycontext-prompt. There is no requirements.txt (the README says pip install numpy scipy scikit-learn).
evidence.verification: Ran `python3.13 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` in research/mimic-anycontext-detect: 5 tests, 5 pass (0.2 s). The tests cover only fit() on a two-family toy where human and machine text differ trivially, auc() with one class, split_half disjointness, and a skippable check that the suite has eight families. None calls regimes(), generator_holdout() or length_matched(), which hold all of the reported results. Mutation: in regimes() I changed `tr = oth + sup` to `tr = oth` and removed the 5x sample weight, so the 'adapted' detector no longer uses any target items and the k = 10/40/160 columns would silently equal the universal column. All 5 tests still passed (mutation survived). Reverted with git checkout (git status clean for the project). Also not tested: the percentile-band logic, the seed handling, or any check that results.txt matches a rerun. The only independent oracle is the reproducibility of results.json, which nothing asserts.
evidence.craft: Read anyctx.py (136 lines), figure.py header, tests/test_anyctx.py in full. Compact and readable, and the leakage trade-offs are disclosed in the README. Defects: the module docstring says 'CPU, about a minute' while the README says about 8 minutes on 4 CPUs; module-level mutable _CACHE keyed by id+label+model string concatenation, rebuilt by prepare() (a second prepare() silently invalidates a scorer built earlier); fit() silently relies on that global; several semicolon one-liners; the TF-IDF vocabulary is fitted on all 4,800 texts including each target (disclosed, but the cheap fix of refitting per regime is not made, and my train-only refit shows the effect is about 0.01 to 0.02 and not in the stated direction); generator_holdout uses one fixed split (seed 0) so it has no spread; no requirements file; no CLI arguments or seed parameter at the command line. No unhandled-input bugs found in the paths run.
evidence.claims: Checked each README claim against a file: 'gap +0.05' and the table (results.txt, recomputed), 'held-out generator AUROC 0.90 to 1.00, lowest wiki/mistral-chat 0.899, abstracts/mistral-chat 0.949' (results.txt lines match), 'raw length alone 0.12 to 0.85' (matches, recomputed wiki and poetry), 'matched deltas' (match), 'per-family sees about 150 human plus about 150 machine texts' (300 human and 157 to 300 machine per family, half each: consistent). Hedges are present and accurate: stylised and preliminary, one detector family, plain-prompt text only, no confidence interval beyond seed spread, produced with AI assistance, no lab endorsement. Not backed: the claim that fitting the vectoriser on all text 'slightly favours the universal regime' (my train-only refit raised recipes from 0.855 to 0.867, so the direction is unverified); 'differences under about 0.01 are within the seed sd' is partly right, but the seed sd (0.002 to 0.017) covers only split randomness, not text sampling, so it understates uncertainty. The README says 'fully stylised' nowhere, but the summary leads with 'preliminary' appropriately.
evidence.fitness: The job: a researcher wants a prompt-free yardstick for how much a detector loses on an unseen context. They get a table, the data pointer (mimic-contexts), a runnable script and a figure, and the README correctly says the prompted-imitator claim is not tested. Gaps that stop it being built on as a result: no confidence intervals over texts (with 150 human and about 150 machine test items per cell, AUROC 0.886 vs 0.896 cannot be ranked); the adapted regime is compared with the universal regime at different training sizes and with an untuned 5x weight; per-family trains on 300 items against 2,100, which the README concedes; the suite has 3 near-identical chat generators, and about 83 of the 273 wiki machine texts share a title (the RAID prompt) with a human text, so halves of a family can share topics across the split (paired titles in suite.jsonl.gz, source_id overlap 83 wiki, 77 recipes). A researcher can reuse it as a baseline row, not as a finding.
evidence.domain: Compared with the cross-domain and cross-model tables in RAID (Dugan et al. 2024), MAGE/DeepfakeTextDetect (Li et al. 2023, out-of-distribution testbeds), M4 (Wang et al. 2024) and the earlier generalisation studies (Bakhtin et al. 2019; Antoun et al. 2023). That literature already shows that supervised detectors lose AUROC on unseen domains and generators and that a small in-domain sample recovers most of it, so the headline (a loss of 0.05 AUROC, closed by 40 to 160 labelled items) is a replication on a small suite with a TF-IDF logistic regression, not a new result; the repository itself says this is a baseline for the real milestone. Departures a detection researcher would flag: single detector family with a stale feature recipe (no transformer fine-tune, no Binoculars/RoBERTa reference), vocabulary fitted on target text, only plain-prompt generations (the attack-free easy end of RAID), no TPR at a fixed 5 percent or 1 percent FPR (RAID's own recommended metric; AUROC hides the deployed operating point), no text-level bootstrap. Sound as a smoke test; not at the standard of a workshop paper.

defects.what: The tests cannot catch a bug in any reported result: they exercise only fit() and helpers on a trivial toy. Deleting the target items from the adapted regime (tr = oth, no 5x weight), which would make k = 10/40/160 equal the universal column, left all 5 tests green. regimes(), generator_holdout() and length_matched() are untested, and nothing asserts results.json against a rerun.

Uncertainty is seed spread only; there is no bootstrap over texts and no TPR at fixed FPR. With about 150 human and 150 machine test items per cell, differences like reddit per-family 0.978 vs universal+160 0.982 are not distinguishable, yet the README's bullets still interpret them. The README's claim that the whole-suite vectoriser 'slightly favours the universal regime' is untested and my train-only refit moved recipes the other way (0.855 to 0.867).

The headline (held-out context loses about 0.05 AUROC and tens of labelled items recover it) is a replication of known cross-domain detector behaviour on a small TF-IDF suite, and does not cite RAID/MAGE/M4 cross-domain results for comparison, only the RAID licence/source.

Module docstring says 'about a minute' but the README says about 8 minutes on 4 CPUs; no requirements.txt; generator_holdout has a single fixed split (no spread); module-global _CACHE keyed by string concatenation.

verdict: Honest, small and reproducible: every number I recomputed (universal books 0.993, wiki 0.895, recipes 0.867 vs 0.843-0.855, wiki per-family, length-alone 0.845 and 0.115, and the means and generator minimum from results.json) agrees with the README within 0.02, the limits are stated up front, and the project is explicit that it is a prompt-free baseline and not the milestone claim. It does not meet the bar because verification is a 1: five toy tests never touch the three functions that produce the results, and a mutation that removes all target adaptation survived. It is also finished but not new (cross-domain detector loss is documented in RAID, MAGE and M4) and carries no text-level confidence intervals or fixed-FPR metric, so a researcher can use it as a baseline row, not build a claim on its differences. The cheapest fix is a test that runs regimes() on a small synthetic or 200-item subset and asserts that adapted k = 160 beats k = 0 when the target family differs, plus a docstring correction.
